**Resubmitted: deviation (WARRANTY), fallback level.**

Repair to the failing period check, in operative language:

- The sub-90-day figure has been removed. Both warranty periods are now at or above 90 days and one is expressed in months: **"for a period of twelve (12) months following delivery"** for conformity of the Site and software to the applicable documentation, and **"for a period of ninety (90) days following performance"** for the services. This satisfies the "≥ 90 days or expressed in months/years" requirement on either reading (minimum period and stated unit).
- Remedy sentence retained and tightened per the earlier polish: repair or replace, or **refund the fees paid for the non-conforming software or services**.
- Also carried the verifier's drafting points: the subsection letter "(c)" is in the operative text, and "its documentation" is now "the applicable documentation" to remove the singular-pronoun ambiguity.

Unchanged: single new subsection; 9(a) and 9(b) untouched and uncontradicted; no survival tail, at-own-expense wording, extra damages categories, notice procedures or disclaimer carve-out; warranty runs from HDI to the Company. Coverage remains the four fallback elements — the preferred workmanlike standard, compliance-with-laws and no-malicious-code warranties are still not sought, and the comment flags that we can discuss shorter periods if HDI pushes back.
